items.stem: You must give a user permission to manage VMs in one resource group only, not anywhere else in the subscription. What should you do?

options.text: Assign Virtual Machine Contributor at the resource group scope
options.rationale: Correct: an RBAC role assigned at resource-group scope applies only to resources in that group.

options.text: Assign Virtual Machine Contributor at the subscription scope
options.rationale: Subscription scope would cover every resource group, which gives too much access.

options.text: Assign Owner at the resource group scope
options.rationale: Owner also lets the user manage access. That breaks least privilege.
Policy controls resource configuration. It does not grant user permissions.

items.explanation: Correct: an RBAC role assigned at resource-group scope applies only to resources in that group.

items.stem: Blobs not accessed for 90 days must move to the cool tier automatically. What do you configure?

options.rationale: Object replication copies blobs between accounts. It does not change their tier.
Correct: lifecycle management rules move blobs between tiers based on age or last access.
Soft delete keeps deleted data. It does not move data between tiers.
Stored access policies control SAS permissions.

items.stem: Which feature lets VMs in two virtual networks talk to each other over the Microsoft backbone without a gateway?

options.rationale: Correct: peering connects VNets with low-latency private connectivity and no VPN gateway.
Service endpoints secure access from a VNet to PaaS services.
UDRs override routing but do not join separate VNets on their own.
Bastion gives browser-based RDP/SSH access to VMs.
